claims.text: The starting low-noble-metal HEA nanoparticles have a near-equiatomic solid-solution structure.
PtPdCoCuNi-based nanoparticles are an example of the proposed low-noble-metal HEA system.
The uncoated nanoparticles are prone to rapid surface diffusion at high temperature.
The uncoated nanoparticles are prone to high-temperature sintering.
An ultrathin porous SiO2 or Al2O3 coating can be applied after synthesis by atomic layer deposition.
The ceramic coating creates an external diffusion barrier.
Controlled coating porosity preserves reactant access to catalytic active sites.
The conformal ceramic coating physically reduces nanoparticle surface-atom mobility.
Reduced surface-atom mobility suppresses particle coarsening.
Reduced surface-atom mobility suppresses elemental segregation.
Suppressing coarsening and segregation preserves the homogeneous near-equiatomic solid-solution structure.
Preservation of the near-equiatomic solid-solution structure is critical for catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
After identical thermal aging, coated nanoparticles will retain a more uniform single-phase structure than uncoated nanoparticles.
After identical thermal aging, coated nanoparticles will undergo less particle coarsening than uncoated nanoparticles.
After identical thermal aging, coated nanoparticles will exhibit less elemental segregation than uncoated nanoparticles.
The coating will enhance nanoparticle stability during high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric operation.
The proposed stabilization applies at 773–1173 K in catalytic service.
The proposed stabilization applies at temperatures up to 1923 K in thermoelectric service.
The proposed benefit requires a coating that balances diffusion resistance against catalytic-site accessibility.
